questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In triangle ABC, CD is the altitude to AB. Prove that a/sin A = b/sin B.
questions.prompt_markup: In triangle ABC, CD is the altitude to AB. Prove that a/sin A = b/sin B.
questions.correct_answer: h = b sin A and h = a sin B, so b sin A = a sin B and a/sin A = b/sin B.
questions.required_method: Write h two ways, using right triangles ADC and BDC.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: sin A = h/b and sin B = h/a from the two right triangles; equate h; divide by sin A sin B. Repeating with another altitude gives c/sin C.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC has an obtuse angle at A, so the altitude from C meets line AB extended past A at D. Prove that a/sin A = b/sin B in this case.

questions.correct_answer: h = b sin(180° - A) = b sin A and h = a sin B, so a/sin A = b/sin B.

questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: the exterior angle at A is 180° - A; h = b sin(180° - A); the identity sin(180° - A) = sin A; equate with h = a sin B.

questions.prompt: Triangle ABC with acute angle A is inscribed in a circle of radius R. Draw the diameter BD. Prove that a/sin A = 2R, and explain why this gives the Law of Sines.
questions.prompt_markup: Triangle ABC with acute angle A is inscribed in a circle of radius R. Draw the diameter BD. Prove that a/sin A = 2R, and explain why this gives the Law of Sines.
questions.correct_answer: ∠BDC ≅ ∠A (inscribed angles on arc BC); ∠BCD = 90°; sin D = BC/BD = a/(2R), so a/sin A = 2R. The same holds for b and c, so all three ratios equal 2R.
questions.required_method: Compare ∠A with ∠D (same arc BC) and use right triangle BCD (angle in a semicircle).
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: inscribed angles on the same arc; angle in a semicircle; sine in right triangle BCD; each ratio equals 2R. (For obtuse A, ∠D = 180° - A and sin D = sin A.)
